status_reason: Values exist for 2015-2024 only and 2025 is not yet published. The publisher warns that pre-2020 rates are not directly comparable with 2020 onward (a sampling change), so the five-year comparison straddles a break in the series. Values are whole percentages read from the report's chart labels; no table or margin of error is published.
name: Poverty rate counting New York costs
definition: Share of New Yorkers whose family resources (after taxes and benefits, minus necessary expenses) fall below a poverty line adjusted for New York City housing costs, from the Poverty Tracker survey's Supplemental Poverty Measure.

source.name: Robin Hood and Columbia University Center on Poverty and Social Policy, The State of Poverty and Disadvantage in New York City, Vol. 8 (March 2026), Figure 1.1, p. 9

source_documents.note: Published only as a FlippingBook viewer (the PDF download asks for an email); the viewer page is cached as a marker, the values were read from the rendered page.

method: No computation. Each annual value is the New York City data label on Figure 1.1 of Vol. 8, page 9, which states: More than 1 in 4 (26%) New Yorkers lived in poverty in 2024, up from 25% the year prior. The 2015-2023 labels match Vol. 7 (Figure 1.1, p. 9) and 2015-2022 match Vol. 6 (Figure 1.1, p. 9).
caveats: Vol. 8, Figure 1.1 note: in 2020 the Poverty Tracker sampling design changed to add an oversample of New Yorkers of Chinese descent, so pre-2020 results are not directly comparable with 2020 onward (the report draws a dashed line between 2019 and 2020).
Vol. 8 says its 2023 rates differ slightly from those in Vol. 7 because of a change in the 2023 sample composition; the rounded citywide 2023 figure (25%) is the same in both.
Survey-based estimate with sampling error; the reports publish no margin of error for the citywide rate, and values are rounded to whole percentages.

Context, not part of this series: the city's own NYCgov poverty measure (Mayor's Office for Economic Opportunity) was 20.5% for 2022, its latest published year, in "New York City Government Poverty Measure 2022: Comprehensive Brief" (July 2025), Table 1, p. 9. It uses American Community Survey data and a different method, so it is not comparable with the Poverty Tracker rate.
No peers: the Poverty Tracker covers New York City only.
